chunks: And 'Asim ibn Humayd narrated from Abu Basir, who said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Shall I tell you about the will of Fatimah (peace be upon her)?' I said: 'Yes.' So he brought out a box or a basket and took out a book from it.

So he read: 'In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.' This is what Fatimah bint Muhammad bequeathed; she bequeathed her seven estates: al-'Awaf, al-Dalal, al-Burqah, al-Mithab, al-Hasna, al-Safiyyah, and the property of Umm Ibrahim, to Ali ibn Abi Talib.

If Ali passes away, then to al-Hasan; if al-Hasan passes away, then to al-Husayn; if al-Husayn passes away, then to the eldest of my children. Allah bore witness to this, along with al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad and al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam.
And Ali ibn Abi Talib wrote.

key_terms.فَاطِمَةُ بِنْتُ مُحَمَّدٍ: Fatimah, daughter of the Prophet Muhammad

ai.seo_question: What were the seven estates bequeathed by Fatimah in her will to Ali and his descendants?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, provides a foundational Shia narrative for the inheritance of the Prophet’s household, detailing Fatimah’s bequest of her seven estates to Ali and subsequently to the Imams in a strict line of succession. The inclusion of witnesses like Al-Miqdad and Al-Zubayr underscores the legal validity of this transfer, reinforcing the Shia doctrine of the Imams' exclusive right to the Prophet's legacy and property. It serves as a key textual evidence for the continuity of spiritual and material authority within the Ahl al-Bayt.
